title: Wicked review:@Joe Weinberg #film #theatre #oscars #academyawards #br...
transcript: in honor of the Oscars this weekend it's time for another theatre-themed movie ranking in the 21st century so far there have been 10 stage to screen adaptations nominated for Best Picture at the Oscars and I'm gonna rank them from worst to best in my own personal opinion before I start just a quick note that I have chosen not to include Moonlight I'm aware of the case to be made for including it but I chose not to in last place I have Les Mis and like look I actually do think there's a lot to like about this movie but it's a mixed bag it's very inconsistent a lot of Tom Hooper's stylistic choices some of the live singing some of the casting choices just really don't hit next up War Horse and you might be thinking is this actually based on the play? or is it just based on the same book that the player is based on? but no, the play is officially credited as one of the source materials for the film I do find this movie very watchable at times it's successful at tugging on the heart strings but it is very schmaltzy and hyper-sentimental often to a fault next up Frost/NIxon based on the Peter Morgan play of the same name this is like a solid political journalism film it's an interesting true story, competently told but it didn't really do much to blow me away I really struggled to rank Fences because of the 10 movies on this list this one has the best material to work with like I adore this play the film is obviously very faithful to the play it's very well acted so in that sense, it's phenomenal and I also really appreciate the mission of this whole project to preserve these stunning works by August Wilson but for the purposes of this list judging it purely as a film I'm not sure that it totally translates the direction feels a little uninspired and it lacks some of that sense of poetry that the writing demands next up The Father which Florian Zeller adapted from his own play of the same name if you don't know this is about a man with dementia but the story is told from his perspective and it almost plays like a horror film I thought this was mostly an effective adaptation it really embraces the medium of film and in some ways it actually works better on film than it did on stage next I have West Side Story and you know obviously Steven Spielberg did a great job with this but I think the real star of the show here is Tony Kushner's screenplay which I think is actually better than the original book of the musical in 4th place I have this year's nominee Wicked which I have a whole video about I'll link it in the caption so you can see my thoughts in more detail but overall, I have some issues with it but they got me next up, Beasts of the Southern Wild based on the play Juicy and Delicious by Lucy Alibar I liked this movie when it first came out but I rewatched it a couple years ago and it just blew me away just like the interplay between the gritty tragedy and the childlike magical realism is endlessly riveting even with a lot of the dark subject matter there's just so much love and joy and beauty in this story and Quvenzhane Wallace absolutely deserved her Oscar nomination second place I will admit this is a bit of a sentimental fave dare I say a problematic fave I have Finding Neverland based on the play The Man Who Was Peter Pan by Alan Knee I grew up watching this on repeat and I have a great fondness for the story of Peter Pan this is another one that is a devastating tragedy but just has this warm magical vibe to it and the story that it's telling historically accurate or not I think is just really beautiful in its own right but in first place you might have seen this coming I have Chicago which not only holds up extremely well it is still the gold standard like the blueprint for how to make a successful musical to movie adaptation in the modern day and people still use it as their go to example for a film adaptation that's better than the original musical so there you go that's my subjective ranking but as always I'm sure you'll tell me how wrong I am in the comments
